merged.rule: kit/07-QUALITY-BAR.md: a set over critics.maxFilesPerMessage is split across two fresh critics with the same rubric and their answers are merged; the merged score is the lower of the two, the issues are both lists in order

issues.where: f0599 to f0600, left skyline and field behind the stem at the 20.00 s cut
issues.what: The stem registers, but the low rain skyline jumps upward into a different left-side ridge and the field boundary shifts with it. The cut reads as a background jump as well as a change in weather and light.
issues.fix: Keep the distant ridge and foreground grass layout registered in the same camera framing on both sides of the cut, then change the lighting, rain and mist in one frame.

issues.where: f0000–f0011, soil clods at the base of the emerging hook and beside the seed coat
issues.what: The hook and seed coat rise between the same intact clods without a visible contact response, so the seedling looks like it is coming through a rigid opening.
issues.fix: Have the advancing hook lift or roll a few adjacent crumbs and let the loose grains settle as the seed coat clears the surface.

issues.where: f0290–f0301, rain around the upper leaves and growing tip
issues.what: The passing streaks are clear, but the wet leaf surfaces do not show a corresponding sequence of strikes, beading or runoff. The rain looks separate from the plant.
issues.fix: Show occasional drops terminating on the leaf surfaces, then beading, kicking off a fine splash or running toward the leaf edges.

issues.where: f0120–f0131, right cotyledon and detached seed coat
issues.what: The right cotyledon opens mostly as a stiff blade rotating at the stem, and the detached seed coat reaches the ground with little visible change in pitch or recoil.
issues.fix: Give the cotyledon a base-to-tip uncurl and add a small tumble and settling response to the seed coat on contact.

issues.where: supplied motion-review pack, across the unit
issues.what: The delivered set has consecutive growth and cut sheets but no whole-segment contact sheet, so the intervening camera, focus and motion continuity cannot be checked.
issues.fix: Include a review-tier or higher overview contact sheet spanning the whole segment in addition to the consecutive-frame sheets.

issues.where: night-to-frost boundary, f0874 to f0925 (29.1–30.8 s); the other world changes are likewise only sparsely sampled
issues.what: No consecutive cut coverage is supplied. The 51-frame gap cannot show whether the plant, grass, and horizon register on the actual cut or the world changes in exactly one frame.
issues.fix: Supply review-tier or higher consecutive frames bracketing each actual cut, with the last outgoing and first incoming frame clearly labeled.

issues.where: rapid bud opening and petal release, f1285 to f1491 (42.8–49.7 s)
issues.what: The sampled poses read as a plausible bloom, but there is no consecutive fast-growth sheet. Frames roughly 1.7 seconds apart cannot distinguish continuous unfolding from a pop or intersection, or reveal brief jitter, focus hunting, or shimmer.
issues.fix: Supply a review-tier or higher strip of consecutive 30 fps frames through the fastest growth stretch, with the entire growing tip visible.
